name: MI-05
label: Likely R

key_factors: Strong Republican district with a PVI of R+13
Walberg is a well-funded incumbent with nearly $1 million on hand
Prediction markets price Walberg around 94% to win
model.rationale: The fundamentals point firmly to Walberg: a heavily Republican-leaning district, incumbency, and a lopsided financial advantage over a minimally funded challenger. Markets agree, pricing his win probability near 94%, so the forecast stays close to the baseline with only a modest tightening.
model.watch: A major outside spending push or an unexpected wave against incumbents could narrow the margin, but nothing in the current evidence suggests it.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Tim Walberg seeks another term in a southern Michigan district that leans Republican by about 13 points at the presidential level. He enters the general election as a heavily funded incumbent, with roughly $1.7 million raised and nearly $1 million in cash, while Democrat Christian Vukasovich has raised under $60,000 and reports modest cash on hand. Minor-party and independent candidates are on the ballot but show no measurable campaign activity.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the money gap, and prediction markets, which give Walberg about a 94 percent chance of winning. The forecast expects a comfortable Republican victory in the mid-teens, with uncertainty wide enough to reflect the absence of polling.
